records.name: The Athenaeum of Philadelphia
records.summary: A member supported library, archive and talk space focused on Philadelphia's books, buildings and history. Members can borrow books, and visitors can join small discussion groups and attend talks.
records.what_you_do: Join a book club, a discussion circle, or a Spanish, French or Italian conversation group, take a database course, or go to a talk. Some groups are free, and others show a price on each listing. Research visits are by appointment.

schedule.text: Book clubs, conversation groups and discussion circles meet on set days and times, mostly weekly or monthly, from Monday to Saturday. Talks and courses are listed by date on the events page.

cost.text: Some groups are free, such as the Spanish, French and Italian conversation groups and some book clubs. Some series show a price, such as $90 to $120 for certain monthly discussion groups. Talks show a price from about $5 to $25. Student membership is $50 a year, Young Friend membership (ages 18 to 35) is $85 a year, the Subscriber level is $160 a year, and a day pass to the reading room is $35.

access.notes: The building has an elevator to all three floors and an accessible restroom on the first floor. Visitors with special needs can enter by a ramp from the rear parking lot and ring the intercom at its top to reach the receptionist. One accessible parking space is in the garden, reached from St. James Street.

first_step.how: Open the events page, pick a discussion group, conversation group or talk, and use its Learn More or Register link. Or call 215-925-2688 to ask how to join.
first_step.basis: Groups and talks are listed publicly with days, times and prices, each with a register link, and a phone line answers questions. The site does not say who may attend each group.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most groups are small circles, such as a book club or conversation group, that meet on a set day and time, and each listing shows its time and price. To see the building first, book a docent-led tour, which runs about 30 to 40 minutes and takes up to 8 people. The site does not say how long a group session runs, so ask when you register.
first_visit_tips: The building is at 219 S. 6th Street, a short walk from Washington Square.
Parking garages are about half a block south on 6th Street: Independence Place (self park) and Hopkinson House (valet).
Hours change by day: open until 7 pm on Monday and 10 am to 3 pm on Saturday. The building also closes on many holidays, such as Thanksgiving and Christmas.
Call 215-925-2688 before you come to ask whether a group is open to non-members, since the site does not say.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the access ramp was step free. The page describes the ramp as an entrance for visitors with special needs and does not say step free, so the wording now matches the page. Who may attend each discussion group is not stated on the site.

records.name: The Brothers Network
records.summary: A group of artists, writers and community members who meet through art and dialogue to support the humanity of Black men. It partners with Moonstone Arts Center on Black Poetry Day in Philadelphia.
records.what_you_do: Attend Black Poetry Day or another public event on the group's list, or give a tax-deductible donation. Events are announced one at a time, so check the events page before you plan a visit.

schedule.text: Programs are announced one at a time. The site describes a Verses and Voices series with 54below and an annual free Race and Sports event, but no regular weekly or monthly meeting.

locations.label: Moonstone Arts Center (Black Poetry Day partner)

cost.text: Some events are free, such as the annual Race and Sports event. Member and friend discounts apply to some partner shows. Donations are optional and tax-deductible.

first_step.how: Pick a public event from the events list and use its RSVP form where one is listed, or call 267-334-4897 to ask how to attend.
first_step.basis: Public events are listed and some ask for an RSVP, but the site describes no membership, classes or volunteer route, and its newsletter form displays a setup message.
first_step.what_to_expect: Each event has its own listing, so check the event page for time, place and cost. The site does not describe how long events run or what a typical evening is like. It also has no accessibility notes for events, so call ahead with access questions.
first_visit_tips: Black Poetry Day is run with Moonstone Arts Center, whose street address is 110A South 13th Street. Check the event listing for the exact room.
Call the office before you come if you need access help, since the site has no accessibility notes for events.

records.notes: Tier 1 gave no street address for the events. The Moonstone site gives 110A South 13th Street, used here as the location. The group's contact page lists no office address, so none is recorded. The newsletter form appears not to be working yet.

records.name: The Chamber Orchestra of Philadelphia
records.summary: A 33 musician chamber orchestra that gives over 30 concerts each season in halls, churches and museums, with talks led by its music director. The public takes part as audience members.
records.what_you_do: Buy tickets to a concert or a lecture, subscribe to a season, or watch select performances live. The jobs and auditions page has no openings right now and does not describe how auditions work.

schedule.text: The orchestra gives more than 30 subscription, neighborhood and education concerts each season, from fall into late spring. Concerts are often weekend pairs at 4 pm, with some Friday evening shows. Lectures are on Sunday afternoons.

locations.label: Kimmel Center for the Performing Arts

cost.text: Single ticket prices are not listed on the site, so check each concert's ticket page. Subscribers get 20 percent off single tickets when they call the box office. Lectures at the Philadelphia Ethical Society cost $25 per person.

access.notes: The Walnut-Locust station on the Broad Street Line is about two blocks from the Kimmel Center. Buses 9, 21, 32 and 42 are listed as wheelchair accessible. The site does not describe step-free entry or elevators at the Kimmel Center, so ask the box office.

first_step.how: Buy a single ticket to any concert online or by calling the box office at (215) 545-1739, or sign up on the site for news and offers.
first_step.basis: Concerts and lectures are open to the public with a ticket, and the site has a clear way to buy in, though it has no first-timer guide.
first_step.what_to_expect: Concerts are given in different places, including halls, churches, museums and cloisters, so check the venue on your ticket. Weekend concerts listed on the site start at 4 pm. Lectures at the Philadelphia Ethical Society run on Sunday afternoons at 2:30 pm and cost $25 per person.
first_visit_tips: Check the venue on your ticket before you go, since concerts move between halls, churches and museums.
If you drive to the Kimmel Center, the garage entrance is just south of the Broad Street entrance, and you can only reach it by driving south on Broad Street.
The Walnut-Locust station on the Broad Street Line is about two blocks away, and buses 9, 21, 32 and 42 run nearby.
Call the box office at (215) 545-1739 to ask about seating or access, since the site does not describe them.

records.notes: Tier 1 called the Walnut-Locust station a Market-Frankford Line stop. The Getting Here page places it on the Broad Street Line, so the record uses that. No interest tag fits a professional orchestra exactly, so community_band is the closest tag.

records.name: The Christian Association Student Community
records.summary: A Christian community at Penn, open to students, staff and neighbors. It offers a weekly Wednesday dinner and discussion, a free online English class, a mentoring program for West Philadelphia high school students, and a monthly Night Church gathering.
records.what_you_do: Come to the Wednesday dinner and discussion, the Thursday English class on Zoom, the Tuesday grad book group, or the monthly Night Church gathering. Ask about the mentoring program if you want to work with high school students.

schedule.text: Wednesday dinner and discussion, 6:30 to 8 pm. Other weekly groups meet on Tuesdays and Thursdays, and Night Church meets on the first Sunday evening of each month.

cost.text: Slanguage, the English class on Zoom, is free. The site gives no price for the dinner or the other groups.

first_step.how: Fill in the visit form on upennca.org or email upennca@gmail.com, and the group will contact you to set a time. You can also join the mailing list.
first_step.basis: The site invites visitors to stop in for a visit through a short form and describes a hospitable community where people can come as they are. It does not say whether belief is required, so this rating covers the first visit only.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Wednesday dinner is a shared meal followed by a discussion of faith and Scripture, from 6:30 to 8 pm. The page does not say where the dinner is held, what it costs, or whether you should bring anything, so ask before you come. Most programs take place at the SPARC building on South 37th Street, so confirm the room first.
first_visit_tips: Send the visit form first, since the group contacts you to set a time.
Ask which room you will meet in, because most programs are at 118 S. 37th St. and the club address is 3637 Chestnut St.
Slanguage meets on Zoom, so you need a phone or computer with internet, and the site points to the group's Facebook page for details.

records.notes: Tier 1 said the group welcomes people of any religious background. Its own pages describe a Christian focus and say visitors can come as they are, without a statement on belief, so the summary and basis now match that. Tier 1 also marked drop-in as yes; the site asks visitors to request a visit first, so drop-in is left out. Slanguage is a program of this group, not a separate group. Night Church comes from the homepage; the what-we-do page does not list it.

records.name: COLOURS Organization
records.summary: A Philadelphia organization for queer people of color that offers health care, HIV and sexual health services, case management and support groups. It also hosts community events such as an open mic night and book clubs, and it makes a video talk series called Conversations.
records.what_you_do: Get free HIV and STI screenings and safer sex kits, use case management, or ask for referrals for mental health care, substance use treatment or PrEP. Ask how to join one of the support groups, or ask about the open mic and book club events. The group also gives out free meals and clothing to people facing hardship.

cost.text: Some services are free, including HIV and STI screenings, safer sex kits, and meals and clothing for people facing hardship. The site gives no price for case management or support groups.

first_step.how: Call 215-832-0100 or email info@coloursorganization.org, or use the contact form on the site, and ask about the service or group you want.
first_step.basis: The site names its services and support groups but does not say who is eligible, how to start, or when groups meet, so the way in is unclear.
first_step.what_to_expect: The services page describes the support groups as spaces to connect and share experiences. It does not give meeting times, group size, or what a first meeting is like, so ask staff when you call.
first_visit_tips: Call before you come, since the site gives no meeting times or intake steps.
The office is at 1211 Chestnut Street, Suite 910, in Philadelphia.

contacts.contact_name: The COLOURS Organization c/o Executive Director

records.notes: Tier 1 named Rainbow Reads as a COLOURS activity. Neither the group's site nor the March 27, 2025 Daily Pennsylvanian article mentions Rainbow Reads, so it is dropped. The article does name an open mic night and book clubs, and the record uses that. The site's footer copyright year is not treated as evidence of activity. An Idealist listing gave a different office address (112 North Broad); the group's own contact page address is used instead.

records.name: Concord School House and Upper Burying Ground
records.summary: Looks after the Upper Burying Ground, a cemetery started in 1693 in Germantown, and the Concord School House, a schoolroom built in 1775 on the cemetery's corner. Visitors can see both during public hours and at summer evening events.
records.what_you_do: Visit the burying ground and the schoolroom during public hours, or come to an event such as the evening Firefly Hours. The site does not list volunteer or membership options.

schedule.text: Public visit hours are posted on the site. Evening Firefly Hours are free outdoor family and nature programs that run April through October at Historic Germantown sites, and this site lists them among its events, usually 5 to 7 pm.

cost.text: Evening Firefly Hours are free, according to the Historic Germantown page that describes them. The homepage gives no price for visiting the burying ground or schoolroom.

first_step.how: Plan a visit during the public hours posted on concordschoolhouse.org, or come to an Evening Firefly Hours event, which is free.
first_step.basis: Public visit hours and events are posted, with no membership step.
first_step.what_to_expect: A visit means walking through the historic burying ground and seeing the 1775 schoolroom during public hours. Firefly Hours are early-evening outdoor programs for families and nature. The site does not say how long a visit takes or how many people usually come.
first_visit_tips: Check the website's visit page for current hours before you go.
Email info@concordschoolhouse.org with access questions, since the site lists none.

records.notes: The visit and events pages on concordschoolhouse.org failed to load (Socket is closed) on every attempt, so visit hours and the full events list are not in this record. Only the homepage of this group was read. The August 2026 Firefly Hours dates from tier 1 are removed from schedule text and kept as last_sign_of_life. Whether this site is one of the participating Historic Germantown sites is inferred from its own events list.

records.name: The Crossing
records.summary: A professional chamber choir that sings only new music, commissioning and premiering new works. Most people take part by attending its concerts or buying its recordings.
records.what_you_do: Go to a concert, buy a ticket for the date you pick, or join the email list. The site does not describe auditions, volunteering, classes or community programs.

schedule.text: A season of concerts, mostly from fall to spring. Several each season are in Philadelphia and Chestnut Hill, and others are in other cities.

cost.text: Tickets are sold for each concert. The season page gives no prices, so check each concert's own ticket page.

first_step.how: Buy a ticket to one of the upcoming concerts, starting with a Philadelphia date, using the link on that concert's own page, or join the email list to hear about new dates.
first_step.basis: Concerts are open to the public, and each date has its own ticket page. The site does not describe any way to sing with the choir, so this rating covers attending only.
first_step.what_to_expect: A concert is a seated performance by a professional choir, often in a church such as St. Mark's in Center City or the Presbyterian Church of Chestnut Hill. The program is new music, and some concerts include other musicians or staging, such as an installation at the Fabric Workshop and Museum. The upcoming page does not give the length of a concert, so check the event page before you buy.
first_visit_tips: Use the ticket link on the concert's own page, since prices and seating are set per event.
Check the start time on your event page, because the season ranges from afternoon to evening starts.
Email info@crossingchoir.org with access questions, since the site lists no access details.

records.notes: Tier 1 had the concerts on Sundays only. The upcoming list shows Friday, Saturday and Sunday concerts with starts from 3 pm to 7 pm, so the days and times are corrected. The 8855 Germantown Avenue address is the group's mailing address, not a concert venue. The concert venues on the upcoming list have no street addresses there, so they are not added as locations. Staff emails were not recorded.

leads_only.name: Moonstone Arts Center
leads_only.note: Partner on Black Poetry Day, named on The Brothers Network site. Runs public poetry readings and has volunteer and intern positions, at 110A South 13th Street. Homepage read once; needs its own tier 1 pass before it becomes a record.

leads_only.name: Historic Germantown
leads_only.note: Runs the Firefly Hours at participating historic sites, including the Concord School House listing. Offers memberships and a pass. Firefly Hours page read once; needs its own record.

leads_only.name: Germantown Historical Society
leads_only.note: Hosts a Firefly Hours greenspace at 5501 Germantown Avenue, per the Historic Germantown page. Not checked; its own site was not fetched.

leads_only.note: Penn student ministry named on the Christian Association's what-we-do page, with a contact email and a listserv. No website of its own found. Not checked.
